AfroBot USA

01

The pilot

AfroBot USA started in McKinney, Texas, in 2024. About 30 students took part. Five to six teams built solutions together, and parents worked closely with them.

02

Teams building together

The teams shared tables and built side by side. This clip and photo are from that day.

03

Families in the room

Parents were in the work with the teams. This is the Build Day group.

04

What we learned

Parents were in the room with the teams. The public record of that day is the film and the photographs on this page. A written account of what the children learned is not on this page yet.

05

What's next

The 2027 season in Dallas–Fort Worth scales the 2024 pilot to about 15 teams and about 90 students. Ages stay on Programs. The hubs stay on Competitions.

Register your interest

2027

The scale-up, and what is only proposed.

The 2027 season in Dallas–Fort Worth scales the 2024 pilot to about 15 teams and about 90 students. The Cameroon program continues, including a Yaoundé event that AfroBot is hosting.

What we are preparing

  • Dallas–Fort Worth. About 15 teams and about 90 students. Small humanoid robots from open-source schematics and 3D-printed parts. Training, safety, and a showcase.
  • Season kickoff in August 2027. That is the published start, not a confirmed venue contract.
  • Yaoundé. AfroBot is hosting. The date is separate from Dallas–Fort Worth, with a two-way livestream between the two places.

Proposed, not confirmed

These are not the 2027 commitment. They need partners before they are real.

  • Washington, DC and Maryland.
  • Atlanta.
  • Houston.
  • A Dallas championship in April 2028. Proposed, pending partner confirmation.
